verdicts.claim: SQLite runs one automatically ... when the WAL holds N or more frames after a commit. The default N is 1000 pages (compile-time SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT)
verdicts.evidence: wal_autocheckpoint.html: 'Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.'

verdicts.claim: NOOP mode (PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP) ... SQLite 3.51.0 (2025-11-04) added it.
verdicts.evidence: 3.51.0 release log: 'Add the PRAGMA wal_checkpoint=NOOP; command and the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP argument for sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2().'

verdicts.claim: WAL-reset bug ... likely present in every version from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09) and is fixed in 3.51.3 (2026-03-13)
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09). It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later.'

verdicts.claim: SQLite 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) ... withdrawn ... 3.53.0 (2026-04-09) re-released 3.52.0 ... first major release that contains the fix
verdicts.evidence: news.html: '2026-04-09 - Version 3.53.0 ... re-release of version 3.52.0 ... first major release (if you don't count 3.52.0) that contains a fix'; '3.52.0 has been withdrawn'; '2026-03-06 - Version 3.52.0'.

verdicts.claim: journal_size_limit (default -1, no limit) makes SQLite truncate the leftover file
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit).'

verdicts.claim: Every checkpoint call first takes the exclusive checkpoint lock ... returns SQLITE_BUSY at once and never invokes the busy handler
verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.'

verdicts.claim: For high write loads, Litestream's tips page recommends PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0
verdicts.evidence: tips: 'it is recommended to run your application with autocheckpointing disabled ... PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 0;' after noting Litestream takes a fresh full snapshot.

verdicts.claim: Antithesis reports its first run found it in 15 minutes ... 3.51.3 came back clean
verdicts.evidence: Antithesis: 'On my first run, Antithesis caught the bug in 15 mins.' ... '3.51.3 comes back clean.'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale's repeated database corruption, first detected by backups in August 2025 ... Antithesis calls it 6 months of shaky uptime
verdicts.evidence: Register: 'in August 2025 those backups began detecting database corruption, repeatedly, with no obvious common trigger'; Antithesis: 'Tailscale suffered 6 months ... of shaky uptime'.

verdicts.claim: Syncthing's developers wrote 'we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader'
verdicts.evidence: Syncthing forum: 'As our application level checkpointer is timer based, we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader.'
